closes: Establishes guard-clause NECESSITY/IRREDUNDANCY for the optimizer-orchestrator deny-by-default authorization contract: all 37 atomic guards are individually load-bearing (necessity rate 1.0000); the well-formed baseline is the unique accepting configuration; the independent clause enumeration exercises all 6 documented attack axes. Reason-level structure beyond the accept/reject decision parity of oracle-parity-v1.

does_not_close: Rust error-taxonomy / exact Err-string parity still requires a live differential harness that executes the Rust runtime and captures its reason strings (Phase-1).

Necessity is shown for the enumerated atomic guards under single-field mutation; it is not an exhaustive 2^N truth table over all guard combinations (interactions are covered only insofar as each guard is independently sufficient to reject).
No product qualification, batch release, procurement, FTO, regulatory, or wet-lab claim; authorization is screening-envelope mediation only.
No promotion, no manifest edit, no scientific_readiness flip (module stays NOT_APPLICABLE / infrastructure lane, solver_use_ceiling DISABLED).
hypothesis: Every atomic guard clause in authorize_optimizer_request is NECESSARY: exactly one configuration (the well-formed baseline) accepts, and each single-clause violation rejects. No redundant (droppable) guard exists; the six documented attack axes are all exercised by the independent clause enumeration.
method_lineage: Extends optimizer-authorization-oracle-parity-v1 along its named does_not_close axis (reason-level structure).
non_circularity: The oracle (optimizer_authorization_oracle.py) is the identical standalone CPython re-implementation used by oracle-parity-v1; its sha256 is pinned below and cross-checked against the sibling study, confirming the contract logic was NOT modified for this study. It does not import, FFI-call, or read the Rust runtime. Necessity is a structural property of the contract verified by constructed minimal cases, not by comparison to any label the oracle itself emits.
purpose: Prove the amphora-optimizer-orchestrator deny-by-default authorization contract is IRREDUNDANT: from one minimal well-formed accepting request/policy/envelope triple, ablating each atomic guard clause by a single-field violation flips the unique accepting configuration to REJECT. Establishes that no guard is removable without admitting an unauthorized row (reference-monitor complete mediation, made constructive), and that the independent clause-set partitions onto all six shipped module-specific attack axes. Strictly stronger than the accept/reject DECISION parity of oracle-parity-v1.
